requirements.statement: The address book lives in the INS frontend at /address-book, reached from an 'Address book' item in the service navigation, and that item is marked active (aria-current) on the list, view and delete pages. 'Log out' stays in the navigation.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts the address book behind the service navigation; DR1's inc-062 ruling already placed the real book in the INS front door rather than the animals frontend.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS frontend serves the list at /address-book (repo-insfrontend-p2-001), its navigation links to it and marks it active on the list, view and delete pages (trace-ins-fit-p2-004, trace-ins-fit-p2-007, trace-ins-fit-p3-069), and the animals dashboard links across to it (repo-tests-p5-001). The navigation's Templates item belongs to the shared layout area.

requirements.statement: A signed-out user opening any address book page is sent to sign in and returned to the page they asked for; a signed-in session with no organisation is refused.
requirements.why: The real address book holds an organisation's records, so it needs an authenticated organisation; the prototype cannot express sign-in.
requirements.deltaNote: Signed-out requests to /address-book and /address-book/add redirect to /auth/sign-in with the path as redirect (trace-e2e-p15-010, trace-e2e-p15-011); a session without an organisation gets 403 (repo-insfrontend-p2-002).

requirements.statement: Address book page titles read '<page heading> - Import notification service - GOV.UK': 'Address book - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the list, '<address name> - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the view page and 'Delete this address? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the delete page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 titles every page with the GOV.UK suffix and a hyphen separator.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the titles are 'Address book | Import notification service', '<name> | Import notification service' and 'Delete address | Import notification service' (trace-ins-fit-p2-008, trace-ins-fit-p2-037, trace-ins-fit-p3-047): a pipe separator and no GOV.UK suffix.

requirements.statement: The list page's heading is 'Address book'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list's h1 is 'Address book' (repo-insfrontend-p2-003, trace-ins-fit-p2-009).

requirements.statement: Under the heading the list page shows, in large body text, 'Manage your addresses for use across all your import notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's intro wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the intro reads 'Manage addresses used across import and export services.' in normal body text (repo-insfrontend-p2-004, trace-ins-fit-p2-010).

requirements.statement: The list page has an 'Add a new address' button (a link styled as a button) to /address-book/add, shown whatever the list holds.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list always shows 'Add a new address' to /address-book/add (repo-insfrontend-p2-010, trace-ins-fit-p2-013).

requirements.statement: On the list page the 'Add a new address' button comes directly under the intro, above the 'Filter addresses' panel and the category tabs.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's order puts adding first and filtering below it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the search form sits between the intro and the 'Add a new address' button (repo-insfrontend-p2-005, repo-insfrontend-p2-010).

requirements.statement: Search and the Type filter sit inside a collapsible 'Filter addresses' disclosure with a chevron, collapsed when the list loads, so the search field is hidden until the user opens it. It is built on the GOV.UK details component, styled to match the design.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tucks filtering away behind one disclosure.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the search form is always visible with no disclosure (repo-insfrontend-p2-005), and the pages use govuk-frontend components only (trace-e2e-p15-037).

requirements.statement: The search field is labelled 'Search'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the field is labelled 'Search addresses' (repo-insfrontend-p2-005, trace-e2e-p15-023).

requirements.statement: The search field's placeholder is 'Search by name, address or country', and it has no hint.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guides the search with a placeholder, not a hint.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the code carries a hint 'Search by name, town or city, postcode or country', passed where the input macro most likely does not render it, and no placeholder (repo-insfrontend-p2-006).

requirements.statement: The search field has an icon-only search button whose accessible name is 'Search', in place of a visible 'Search' text button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search control.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a primary text button 'Search' submits the form (repo-insfrontend-p2-007, trace-e2e-p9-089). What pressing the icon does is settled with the search mechanism in c-address-book-list-002.

requirements.statement: Search matches the trimmed text, case-insensitively and anywhere inside a word, against an address's name, type labels, every address line (line 1, line 2, town or city, county, postcode), its transporter approval number and its country name; a blank search is no search.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 searches the whole visible row, so 'Ballymore' or a country finds the entry; today only name, town and postcode match.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book API's q matches only name, town or city and postcode (repo-addressbook-p3-032, repo-addressbook-p3-033), and a country is found only when the whole term resolves to a country name, which the INS frontend turns into an OR countryCode filter (repo-insfrontend-p2-009). Case-insensitive, partial, literal, trimmed matching already holds (repo-addressbook-p3-034 to p3-039).

requirements.statement: The address book API keeps its countryCode filter as it is: an exact, trimmed ISO alpha-2 code, ignored when blank, organisation-scoped, leaving out deleted addresses, and combined with q by OR.
requirements.why: The locked contract and ruling cv-048 fix these semantics; nothing in Design Release 2.1 asks to change them.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven by the address book's AddressSearchIT and OperatorServiceTest (repo-addressbook-p3-064 to p3-066, repo-addressbook-p3-074, repo-addressbook-p3-075).

requirements.statement: Searching and choosing a Type filter the current category's addresses across all its pages as the user types or chooses, without a separate apply button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 filters live, with no submit or apply button on the filter.
requirements.deltaNote: Today search is a server-side GET form submitted by a Search button, and the API answers one server-sized page at a time (repo-insfrontend-p2-005, repo-insfrontend-p2-068, repo-addressbook-p3-010).

requirements.statement: While a search or Type filter is active the results line describes the matches (for example 'Showing 1-2 of 2').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the count true to what is shown while filtering.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the results line already counts only matches after a submitted search (repo-addressbook-p3-047, repo-insfrontend-p2-014); whether it updates live, and whether pagination hides as the prototype's does, follows c-address-book-list-002.

requirements.statement: The list is split into four category tabs, in this order: 'Origin and Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer', 'Transporter' and 'Branch'; each tab is a link to /address-book?category=origin-and-consignor, destination-consignee-importer, transporter or branch, and the selected one is marked.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 groups addresses by what they are used for.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list is one table with no tabs (trace-e2e-p15-026), and the API has no type or usage filter to split by (repo-addressbook-p3-046). The address type each record carries comes from the add-and-edit area's typed record.

requirements.statement: Each tab panel has its own heading: 'Origin and Consignor addresses', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer addresses', 'Transporter addresses' or 'Branch addresses'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads each category's table.

requirements.statement: An address appears on every tab whose category holds any of its types: Origin and Consignor holds place of origin, consignor, consignor or exporter and exporter; Destination, Consignee and Importer holds consignee, importer, place of destination, contact and packer; Transporter holds transporters; Branch holds branch addresses. So an address with several types can appear on more than one tab, and the list API can return one category's addresses.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists an organisation under each use it is held for.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's record carries no type (repo-tests-p5-095, trace-e2e-p15-082, repo-insfrontend-p2-070) and the list has no type or category filter (repo-addressbook-p3-046).

requirements.statement: With no category in the URL, or an unknown one, the list opens on the Origin and Consignor tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's default tab.

requirements.statement: Each tab link goes to page 1 of that category, keeps the current search and drops the Type filter; the filter form carries the selected category as a hidden field so filtering stays on the current tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps a search across tabs but not a type, which is per category.

requirements.statement: The legacy category values origin-and-sender and destination-and-receiver are not accepted as aliases.
requirements.why: They exist only so the prototype's older design releases keep working; the real service never used those values, so there are no links to keep alive.

requirements.statement: The filter has a select labelled 'Type' whose first option is 'Select one' (empty value), then options for the current tab only: 'Place of Origin' and 'Consignor' on Origin and Consignor; 'Consignee', 'Importer' and 'Place of Destination' on Destination, Consignee and Importer; 'Commercial' and 'Private' on Transporter; 'Branch Address' on Branch.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 narrows a tab by type.
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no type filter in the page or the API (repo-addressbook-p3-046).

requirements.statement: The Type filter keeps a transporter whose transporter type (Commercial or Private) equals the choice, and any other address when one of its types equals the choice; the list API takes the type and category so the filter runs over the whole category, still organisation-scoped and without deleted addresses.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's type matching, delivered over the real, paged book.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list API's only filters are q and countryCode, every path pinned to ACTIVE and the caller's organisation (repo-addressbook-p3-046, repo-addressbook-p3-027).

requirements.statement: Above the table a results line reads 'Showing <start>-<end> of <total>'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list shows 'Showing <from>-<to> of <total>' (repo-insfrontend-p2-014, trace-ins-fit-p2-015).

requirements.statement: When nothing matches, or the book or tab is empty, the list shows 'Showing 0 of 0' and an empty table, with no empty-state or no-match message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the same table whatever it holds.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an empty book shows 'You have no addresses yet.' and a search with no match shows 'No addresses match "<term>".', each in place of the table and with no results line (repo-insfrontend-p2-012, repo-insfrontend-p2-013, trace-ins-fit-p2-034).

requirements.statement: The list has no 'Clear search' link; the user clears the search field instead.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's filter has no clear control.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a 'Clear search' link to /address-book shows above the results of a search and under a no-match message (repo-insfrontend-p2-013, repo-insfrontend-p2-015).

requirements.statement: On every tab except Transporter the table's columns are Name, Type, Address and Country, then an action column whose header 'Action' is visually hidden.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows what each address is used for.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the columns are Name, Address, Country and the hidden Action, with no Type column (repo-insfrontend-p2-016, trace-e2e-p15-026).

requirements.statement: On the Transporter tab the table's columns are Name, Address, Approval number and Type, then the hidden Action column, with no Country column: the country is the address's last line, the approval number reads like 'RO/BUCHAREST/T1/00092010', and Type is 'Commercial' or 'Private'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows transporters by approval and type.

requirements.statement: In the Name column a name of more than one word is shown on two lines: the first word, then the rest.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's Name cell.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the Name cell shows the name on one line (repo-insfrontend-p2-017).

requirements.statement: In the Address column every stored address line (line 1, line 2, town or city, county, postcode) is shown on its own line, each but the last ending in a comma; blank lines are left out.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the whole address, line by line.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the cell joins only address line 1, town or city and postcode into one comma-separated line, leaving out line 2 and county (repo-insfrontend-p2-018, trace-e2e-p15-027).

requirements.statement: The Country column shows the country's name, not its code.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list looks up the country name, falling back to the code (repo-insfrontend-p2-019, trace-e2e-p15-028).

requirements.statement: The Type column shows the address's type labels joined by ', ', using the list's labels: 'Place of origin', 'Consignor' (for consignor, consignor or exporter and exporter), 'Consignee', 'Importer', 'Place of destination', 'Transporter', 'Branch', 'Contact address' and 'Packer'. These differ in case and wording from the Type filter's options.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 labels uses in sentence case in the table.

requirements.statement: Each row ends with a 'View' link to /address-book/{id}; its accessible name adds the address's name in visually hidden text ('View <name>').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's row action; the hidden name keeps each link distinct for screen reader users.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list already ends each row with 'View' plus the hidden name (repo-insfrontend-p2-020, trace-ins-fit-p2-021).

requirements.statement: The list shows 8 addresses a page, set through the address book service's server-side page size setting.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 pages at 8; ruling cv-025 keeps page size a server setting, so the setting changes rather than the contract.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book pages at 25 because address-book.list.page-size is unset (repo-addressbook-p3-011), and the INS list shows 25 a page (trace-ins-fit-p2-023, trace-e2e-p15-030).

requirements.statement: When there is more than one page, GOV.UK pagination shows a numbered link to every page with the current one marked, 'Previous' except on the first page and 'Next' except on the last; with one page there is no pagination.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list already renders GOV.UK pagination this way (repo-insfrontend-p2-021, trace-ins-fit-p2-024 to p2-029).

requirements.statement: Pagination links keep the category, search and Type filter, and add page only for pages after the first.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the user's tab and filters as they page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the links keep q and countryCode and add page only after the first (repo-insfrontend-p2-022); there is no category or type to keep.

requirements.statement: A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and one beyond the last page shows the last page's addresses.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never shows an empty page for a stale page link.
requirements.deltaNote: A missing, non-numeric or sub-1 page already means page 1 (repo-insfrontend-p2-011), but a page beyond the last gets an empty items list from the API (repo-addressbook-p3-017) while only the label and pagination are clamped (repo-insfrontend-p2-023).

requirements.statement: The list shows the newest address first, with a stable order from page to page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists the user's latest additions first; the real API already sorts newest first.
requirements.deltaNote: The API sorts by creation time, newest first, ties by id (repo-addressbook-p3-028, repo-addressbook-p3-029); a newly saved address lands in the first row (trace-e2e-p15-031).

requirements.statement: After an add, edit or delete the list shows a GOV.UK success notification banner titled 'Success' above the heading, once: it is cleared when read.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list shows the session's success message once in a 'Success' banner (repo-insfrontend-p2-028, repo-insfrontend-p2-029).

requirements.statement: The success banner stays on the page; it does not hide itself after a few seconds.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's banner stays until the user moves on, so slower readers do not miss it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today client JavaScript hides the banner 3 seconds after load (repo-insfrontend-p2-030).

requirements.statement: After a delete the banner reads '<Name> address deleted', with the name's first letter capitalised and the rest lower-cased (for example 'Green valley farm address deleted'), or 'Address deleted' when the name is blank.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's delete confirmation wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner reads '<name> deleted from your address book', name as typed (repo-insfrontend-p2-031, trace-e2e-p15-035).

requirements.statement: The address book is stored by the address book service and belongs to the organisation: every user signed in to the same organisation sees the same addresses, and one user's additions and deletions show for the others.
requirements.why: Persistence and organisation scoping are real constraints the prototype, which holds the book in one user's session, cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The service scopes by organisation only, with no user identity (repo-addressbook-p4-003); E2E proves another user in the organisation sees adds and deletes (trace-e2e-p15-077, trace-e2e-p15-078).

requirements.statement: Address book additions, edits and deletions held only in the user's session, with no address book API behind them.
requirements.why: Set aside by c-address-book-list-005: the real book is persisted and organisation-wide.

requirements.statement: No caller can list, read or delete another organisation's addresses: the path organisation must match the caller's organisation header exactly, and any miss, whether unknown or another organisation's, is the same 404, never 403.
requirements.why: Organisation isolation and non-disclosure are real authorisation constraints (rulings cv-010 and cv-040).
requirements.deltaNote: Proven in the address book's AddressScopingIT and IdentityHeaderFilterTest (repo-addressbook-p4-053, repo-addressbook-p4-054, repo-addressbook-p4-059); no E2E spec signs in as a second organisation (repo-tests-p5-097).

requirements.statement: Every address book API call must carry a well-formed Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header (1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens); a missing, blank or malformed one is refused with a 400 problem response with no errors map, before any handler runs, and a new address is stamped with that organisation.
requirements.why: The header is the address book's only tenant key.
requirements.deltaNote: IdentityHeaderFilter enforces it on every /organisation/ path (repo-addressbook-p4-006, repo-addressbook-p4-010, repo-addressbook-p4-044).

requirements.statement: The INS frontend calls the address book server-side under /organisation/{orgId}/addresses with the signed-in session's organisation in the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header and the trace id, and refuses to call it without an organisation.
requirements.why: The address book trusts the header alone, so it must come only from the authenticated session (ruling cv-010).
requirements.deltaNote: The INS client sets the header from the session and fails before sending without one (repo-insfrontend-p2-065, repo-insfrontend-p2-067).

requirements.statement: The address book's trust boundary outside the service: stripping a client-sent organisation header, setting it from the verified session, CDP network policy, and the service's own resource-server authentication.
requirements.why: Platform and deployment controls the Design Release 2.1 programme does not change; it goes to the report as a standing risk nothing in the repo proves.

requirements.statement: The address book service logs each request with the caller's organisation id and no address personal data, logs list requests without the search term, and times the list endpoint and its query as metrics.
requirements.why: Operability without leaking personal data.
requirements.deltaNote: IdentityHeaderFilter and OperatorController already do this (repo-addressbook-p4-036, repo-addressbook-p3-048, repo-addressbook-p3-049).

requirements.statement: The list API (GET /organisation/{orgId}/addresses) returns a camelCase page object with items, page, pageSize, totalItems and totalPages, holds only live addresses, and answers errors as application/problem+json.
requirements.why: The real list contract the INS frontend reads.
requirements.deltaNote: OperatorPageResponse and OperatorListIT (repo-addressbook-p3-018, repo-addressbook-p3-053).

requirements.statement: Reading one address by id returns it with every stored field, including a deleted one with deleted true; only that tells a caller the address was deleted, and a 404 means unknown or not this organisation's.
requirements.why: Notifications keep referring to addresses after they are deleted, so deletion must stay detectable.
requirements.deltaNote: AddressGetIT proves 200 with deleted true for a tombstone and 404 for an unknown id (repo-addressbook-p2-033, repo-addressbook-p2-034).

requirements.statement: Deleting an address removes it from the list and search for everyone in the organisation but keeps it as a tombstone (deleted, name intact, readable by id); delete answers 204, is idempotent, cannot be undone, and is reached in the interface only through the delete confirmation page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 removes the address from the book; the tombstone is the real persistence constraint that stops notifications referencing it from dangling.
requirements.deltaNote: The service soft-deletes and answers 204 idempotently (repo-addressbook-p2-053, repo-addressbook-p2-058); E2E proves the tombstone (trace-e2e-p15-075).

requirements.statement: The address view page is at /address-book/{id}, headed with the address's name, and can be opened directly by its URL.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page is served at /address-book/{id} with the name as h1 (repo-insfrontend-p2-032, repo-insfrontend-p2-038).

requirements.statement: The view page's summary list always shows, in this order, 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Town or city', 'Postcode or Zip code', 'Country' (as a name), 'Email address' and 'Phone number'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on these rows.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page shows these rows in this order (repo-insfrontend-p2-040, trace-ins-fit-p2-039).

requirements.statement: The view page shows 'Address line 2 (optional)' after Address line 1, and the county row after Town or city, only when they have a value.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leaves empty optional rows out.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both rows always show, blank when empty (repo-insfrontend-p2-049, trace-ins-fit-p2-041).

requirements.statement: The view page's county row is labelled 'County (optional)'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the row is labelled 'County' (repo-insfrontend-p2-045, trace-ins-fit-p2-042).

requirements.statement: The view page does not show the address's types or uses, and its summary rows have no Change links: the whole address is changed through the Edit button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page has no type row and no Change links (repo-insfrontend-p2-040, repo-insfrontend-p2-050).

requirements.statement: The view page's 'Edit' button, to /address-book/{id}/edit, is a secondary button, beside the Delete button in a button group.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 styles Edit as secondary.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Edit is a primary (green) button-link to /address-book/{id}/edit (repo-insfrontend-p2-051).

requirements.statement: The view page has a red warning 'Delete' button to /address-book/{id}/delete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page has a warning 'Delete' button-link (repo-insfrontend-p2-052, trace-ins-fit-p2-045).

requirements.statement: With no return path, the view page's Back link goes to the address book list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page's Back link goes to /address-book (repo-insfrontend-p2-039, trace-ins-fit-p2-047).

requirements.statement: The view and delete pages honour a return query: the view page's Back link goes to it, its Edit and Delete links carry it on, the delete page's Back and 'No, cancel' carry it to the view page, and after a delete the user goes to it unless it is one of the deleted address's own pages, when they go to the list. A return path is honoured only when it starts with a single /.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the user back to where they opened the address from, such as a notification page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the view page's Back always goes to the list and a delete always lands on the list (repo-insfrontend-p2-039, repo-insfrontend-p2-061).

requirements.statement: Opening the view page for an id that is not a live address in the organisation's book (unknown, malformed, another organisation's or deleted) sends the user to the view page's back link (the return path or the list) rather than a 404 page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 redirects a dead address link instead of showing an error.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a malformed id, an unknown or other organisation's id and a deleted address all respond 404 Page not found (repo-insfrontend-p2-033, repo-insfrontend-p2-035, repo-insfrontend-p2-036).

requirements.statement: Opening the delete page for an id that is not a live address in the book redirects to the return path or the list; posting a delete for such an id changes nothing, shows no banner and redirects as a delete would.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 treats a stale delete as a no-op rather than an error.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete page and its POST respond 404 when the address is missing or deleted (repo-insfrontend-p2-061, repo-insfrontend-p2-062).

requirements.statement: The address view page showing addresses found outside the book (a notification's consignment, contact or transporter addresses), without Edit or Delete.
requirements.why: Set aside by c-address-book-list-006: those addresses are copies held by the notification service, not the address book, so the INS view page reads the book only.

requirements.statement: When the address book service fails unexpectedly, the list renders the shared recoverable error banner with no table, and the view and delete pages respond with the service error page; each failure is logged.
requirements.why: A real cross-service failure the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list renders 'There is a problem' on failure and the view and delete pages respond 500 (repo-insfrontend-p2-025, repo-insfrontend-p2-037, repo-insfrontend-p2-062).

requirements.statement: The list renders in the wide display column; the view and delete pages in the two-thirds column; every page keeps the skip link and the standard GOV.UK footer.
requirements.why: Today's layout; nothing in Design Release 2.1 changes it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p2-027 and repo-insfrontend-p2-038-m1 set the columns; trace-ins-fit-p2-002-m1 shows the footer.

requirements.statement: The list, view and delete pages have no serious or critical axe violations against WCAG 2.0 A/AA, 2.1 A/AA and 2.2 AA after the changes.
requirements.why: Accessibility is a legal requirement for the service.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS fit suite runs axe on each page and passes today (repo-insfrontend-p2-085, repo-insfrontend-p2-092, repo-insfrontend-p2-096).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation is served by GET and POST at /address-book/{id}/delete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree; Design Release 2.1 overrides only this address book view.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS delete page is served at /address-book/{id}/delete by GET and POST (repo-insfrontend-p2-053).

requirements.statement: The delete page's heading is 'Delete this address?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's heading.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the heading is 'Delete address' (repo-insfrontend-p2-054, trace-ins-fit-p3-046).

requirements.statement: The delete page shows a summary list with one row, 'Address', holding the name, each address line and the country on separate lines, leaving out any line that repeats one already shown (ignoring case) and never the email or phone; with none of those it shows 'Not applicable'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows what is being deleted before the user confirms.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete page shows only the address's name, in its question (repo-insfrontend-p2-056).

requirements.statement: Below the summary the delete page says 'Confirm that you want to delete this address.', in place of today's 'Are you sure you want to delete <name> from your address book?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording; the name now shows in the summary.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page asks 'Are you sure you want to delete <name> from your address book?' with the name in bold (repo-insfrontend-p2-055, trace-ins-fit-p3-048).

requirements.statement: The delete page warns 'This action cannot be undone.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 warns the user; it is true, as the API has no restore.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's page has no such warning (repo-insfrontend-p2-055).

requirements.statement: The delete page's confirm button is a red warning button reading 'Yes, delete'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's button text.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the button reads 'Yes, delete this address' (repo-insfrontend-p2-059, trace-ins-fit-p3-050).

requirements.statement: Beside the confirm button the delete page has a 'No, cancel' link to the address's view page, deleting nothing and showing no banner.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers cancel as a link, not a second button.
requirements.deltaNote: Today cancel is a secondary submit button 'Cancel' (cancel=true) that redirects to the view page (repo-insfrontend-p2-060, trace-ins-fit-p3-051).

requirements.statement: With no return path, the delete page's Back link goes to the address's view page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS delete page's Back goes to /address-book/{id} (repo-insfrontend-p2-057).

requirements.statement: Confirming the delete deletes the address through the address book service and, with no return path, lands on the list, where the address no longer appears and the count drops by one.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS POST deletes through the service and redirects to /address-book, where the row is gone (repo-insfrontend-p2-061, trace-e2e-p15-074).

requirements.statement: The delete form is protected by a CSRF token and posts nothing else.
requirements.why: A real security constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS delete form carries a crumb token (repo-insfrontend-p2-058, trace-ins-fit-p3-068).

requirements.statement: Deleting an address makes no check on whether a notification uses it and shows no in-use warning.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree; the tombstone keeps those notifications' references whole.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS delete proceeds unconditionally (repo-insfrontend-p2-109).

requirements.statement: The INS frontend's in-memory address book stub behaves like the real list: 8 a page, filtering by search, category and Type, and soft-deleting so a deleted address reads back as deleted.
requirements.why: The fit suite runs against the stub, so it must exercise the Design Release 2.1 list rather than today's.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the stub pages at 25, ignores the search term and country code, and deletes outright (repo-insfrontend-p2-078, repo-insfrontend-p2-079, repo-insfrontend-p2-081).

requirements.statement: Every new or changed English string on the list, view and delete pages has a Welsh counterpart, kept marked as an unreviewed machine draft until it has Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: The INS frontend carries Welsh copy for every address book string; leaving the old Welsh would show users a different page in Welsh.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's Welsh copy matches today's English: 'Rheoli cyfeiriadau a ddefnyddir ar draws gwasanaethau mewnforio ac allforio.', 'Chwilio cyfeiriadau', 'Dileu cyfeiriad' and so on (repo-insfrontend-p2-099 to p2-105).

requirements.statement: The tests repo's shared address book fixtures each carry an address type, so they land on the right category tab and the journey parties still find them, and the pre-run reconcile treats a missing or drifted type as drift.
requirements.why: Once the list is split by type, untyped fixtures would sit on no tab and the E2E specs that find them would break.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the 13 shared fixtures are reconciled by name and hold no type (repo-tests-p5-118, repo-tests-p5-121-m1).

requirements.statement: End-to-end specs walk the address book through its own links (list, category tab, search, View, Delete, 'No, cancel', 'Yes, delete') rather than opening view and delete pages by URL, and cover the empty and no-match state.
requirements.why: Today no spec proves the user can reach view or delete from the list, or that search works.
requirements.deltaNote: Every spec opens view, edit and delete by URL (repo-tests-p5-109-m1), and no spec or trace drives search (repo-insfrontend-p2-106, trace-e2e-p15-039).

requirements.statement: The prototype's seeded demonstration addresses (its farms, transporters, three Defra branches, multi-type entries and padding copies) and their ids.
requirements.why: Demonstration data: the real book holds each organisation's own records.

requirements.statement: DR1's own address book screens and the animals frontend's navigation into them.
requirements.why: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements (the ruling), and inc-062 struck DR1's address book screens; Design Release 2.1 governs the INS book's design.

requirements.statement: Closing the address book service's own test gaps: no test proves the countryCode filter is case-sensitive, nor that q leaves out county, address line 2, phone and email.
requirements.why: A test-coverage gap in a contract this programme does not change; it goes to the report.

conflicts.about: Address book page size: Design Release 2.1's 8 against today's 25.

positions.says: The list shows 8 addresses a page.
The list shows 8 addresses a page.
The page size is a server setting, address-book.list.page-size, unset and so 25.
The INS list shows 25 addresses a page.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins: 8 a page. Ruling cv-025 (page size is server configuration, not a request parameter) is kept by setting address-book.list.page-size to 8 rather than adding a parameter. Nothing is overruled: today's claims stay as the evidence of what changes.

conflicts.about: How live filtering works: the prototype holds every row of a category in the page and filters it in the browser; the real list is served one server-sized page at a time by the address book API.

positions.says: The search button does not submit; a client-side module filters every entry the page carries as JSON.
Typing sends no request, so all a category's rows must already be in the page; pagination hides while filtering.
The list is paged on the server with a server-set page size and no way to ask for everything.
Search is a GET form submitted with a Search button, answered by the API's q.
The ruling does not say whether, where a real constraint overrides, the service keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as it can.

conflicts.outcome: The visible behaviour (filter as you type across the whole category, no apply button, count of matches) is the prototype's and wins, but the prototype's mechanism of loading every row into the page cannot carry over to a server-paged, organisation-sized book without either fetching the whole category on every page load or searching on the server. Two readings build different things in the INS frontend and the address book API, and neither precedence nor a ruling picks one.
conflicts.question: Should the INS address book filter as the user types by loading a category's every address into the page and filtering in the browser, as the prototype does, or by searching on the server through the address book API?
conflicts.default: Search on the server. The filter stays a GET form to /address-book carrying category, search and type; the address book API filters a whole category by q (the widened fields) and type and returns 8 a page. Without JavaScript, pressing Enter in the search field or choosing a type and pressing Enter submits it. With JavaScript, the page re-requests the list as the user types or changes Type (debounced) and swaps in the table, results line and pagination without a full reload. While filtering, the results line counts the matches and pagination shows only when the matches run past 8. Same locally, in the stub, on the compose stack and in CDP.

conflicts.about: Return paths into the address book: the prototype's return query is a same-site path, but in the real service the pages that link into the book with a return (the animals journey) are on another origin.

positions.says: A return path is honoured only when it starts with a single /; anything else falls back to the list.
The animals frontend and the INS address book are on different origins.
The view page's Back always goes to the address book list.

conflicts.outcome: Within the INS frontend the prototype's rule can be built as written. A return to an animals journey page, the prototype's main reason for the return query, cannot be a same-origin path, and accepting another origin is a cross-service and open-redirect decision the prototype cannot express.
conflicts.question: When an animals journey page links to an INS address book page with a return, should INS send the user back to the animals frontend, which is on another origin?
conflicts.default: Yes, but only to the configured animals frontend origin: INS honours a return that starts with a single / as an INS page, as the prototype does, and an absolute URL whose origin exactly equals the configured animals frontend origin; anything else falls back to the list (view page) or the view page (delete page). Locally, on the compose stack and in CDP the allowed origin is each environment's animals frontend base URL; in the INS stub mode only same-origin paths are honoured.

conflicts.about: Controls and states today's INS list has that Design Release 2.1 does not: the empty-state and no-match messages, the Clear search link and the banner that hides itself.

positions.says: Wherever a real service differs from Design Release 2.1, it changes to match.
When nothing matches the list shows an empty table and 'Showing 0 of 0', with no message.
The filter's only button is the search icon; there is no clear control.
The success banner is shown once and cleared, with no timed hide.
An empty book shows 'You have no addresses yet.'
A search with no match shows 'No addresses match "<term>".' and a Clear search link.
A search with results shows a Clear search link.
The success banner hides itself after 3 seconds.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling and the prototype outrank the INS frontend: these are differences from Design Release 2.1 and none rests on persistence, validation, authentication or cross-service behaviour, so they go. The ruling's own open point on behaviour Design Release 2.1 does not show at all does not apply: the prototype shows its empty, search and banner states. Today's claims are not listed as overruled because the change requirements cite them as the evidence of what is removed.

conflicts.about: Where the address book is kept: the prototype holds it in one user's session; the real book is persisted by the address book service and shared by the organisation.

positions.says: Additions, edits and deletions are held in the user's prototype session only.
No address book API is called; entries live in the session.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence, overrides it.
The book is scoped by organisation only, so every user of the organisation sees and changes the same book.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's persistence constraint wins: the book stays persisted in the address book service and organisation-wide. The prototype's session-only storage is set aside; what the user sees on each page is still the prototype's.

conflicts.about: Whether the address view page shows addresses found outside the book (a notification's consignment, contact or transporter addresses).

positions.says: The view page shows any address the service knows by id, looking in the book and then consignment, contact and transporter addresses.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as cross-service behaviour, overrides it.
The view page reads the address book service only, and anything it does not hold is not found.

conflicts.outcome: The cross-service constraint wins: a notification's addresses are copies held by the notification service, not the address book, so the INS view page reads the book only. How a notification shows its own addresses belongs to the journey areas.

conflicts.about: The row's View link: the prototype's bare 'View' against today's 'View <name>' with the name visually hidden.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
Each row ends with a 'View' link.
Each 'View' link adds the address name in visually hidden text.

conflicts.outcome: Sighted users see the same 'View' either way. The hidden name meets the accessibility regulations the service must satisfy (distinct link purpose for screen reader users), a real constraint a visual prototype does not express, so it is kept. Nothing is overruled: the prototype's View link is built.

conflicts.about: The service navigation's items: the prototype shows Dashboard, Templates, Address book and Manage account; today's INS navigation also has Log out and no Templates.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as authentication, overrides it.
The navigation shows Dashboard, Templates, Address book and Manage account.
The navigation shows a Log out link to /auth/sign-out.

conflicts.outcome: Signing out is an authentication constraint the prototype cannot express, so Log out stays. The prototype wins on the rest: Address book is the active item on its pages here, and the Templates item is the shared layout area's change. Nothing is overruled.
